sections.overview: Nomada argentata is a European cuckoo bee whose known host is the mining bee Andrena marginata; its life depends on that bee’s nesting sites.
sections.identification: An Irish account describes a small to medium bee with a red-and-black abdomen and grey hairs at the thorax base; field identification should be checked against a specialist key.
sections.habitat: It occurs in open grasslands where A. marginata and its food plants, especially scabiouses and Succisa, are present; the Italian assessment includes both dry and damp meadows.
sections.diet: Like other Nomada, the female does not provision a nest with pollen: the larva exploits the host bee’s brood cell and stored food.
sections.behavior: Adults may visit scabious flowers, but these visits do not make the bee a pollen-provisioning species; compare N. atroscutellaris, another specialist tied to a single Andrena host.
sections.reproduction: The female lays in nests of A. marginata; accounts identify this host relationship, but details of egg laying and larval timing are not established here.
sections.ecology: Its dependence on A. marginata links it to grasslands with scabiouses and Succisa, so loss of these host-rich meadows can affect both bees.
sections.conservation: The European Red List assesses N. argentata as Vulnerable, while an Italian assessment gives Near Threatened; these are separate geographic assessments, not a global category.
